html:
From the 1950s Andorra turned from a poor land of shepherds and smugglers into a centre of duty-free shopping, skiing and banking. Millions of visitors a year now cross its borders.

Low taxes on goods drew shoppers from France and Spain for tobacco, alcohol and electronics. A road network and ski resorts brought tourists, and the population grew several times over with workers from Spain, Portugal and France. Banks and low taxes also made it a tax haven.

Since the 2010s Andorra has signed agreements with the European Union to share tax information and has introduced income tax, under pressure to drop its tax haven status. It uses the euro without being an EU member. See Andorra.
